groups.subject: State publication
observations: Prepared blobs do not become visible until revision-fenced KeeperMap publication; strict mode, synchronous insertion and wait_end_of_query are forced by storage transport
Multi-record reads confirm heads before and after value reads; missing or mismatched blobs fail closed rather than becoming null
Compaction republishes the same content at a newer revision before deleting obsolete history, preserving stale-writer fences

groups.subject: Investigation writer and progress ownership
observations: Budget transforms and progress publication acquire the same per-investigation writer; publication includes the held writer revision and releases it atomically with updated records
Acquisition verifies token and expiry; abandoned acquisition or cancelled publication schedules bounded cleanup only when the stored token still belongs to the cancelled owner
Progress checks job id, worker, attempt, running state and strictly live lease after elapsed wait; stale owners cannot publish a review checkpoint

groups.subject: Budget and cancellation
observations: Reservation admission rechecks active job ownership and attempt under storage lock; held live current-month amounts reduce remaining capacity without charging them
Settlement removes the reservation by identity and is therefore idempotent, charges the originating job, and does not add old-month cost to a new month

Cancellation cleanup carries already observed provider cost and step; pre-response cancellation releases unused allowance. Provider behavior and unknown cost after network loss are outside synthetic test guarantees

groups.subject: Eval and signal lease ownership
observations: Eval renewal validates a matching live token and cannot shorten its stored deadline; completion atomically seals the run, clears its scoring index and writes the baseline reference
Signal completion requires both the same configuration fingerprint and exact persisted claim deadline; a replaced claim is not overwritten

groups.subject: Credential revocation and migration
observations: Tracing-key catalog creation and revocation retry revision conflicts against the latest catalog; creation cannot replace an existing key identity
Importer obtains all eight Lens source groups in one repeatable-read read-only transaction and validates the complete plan before target setup

Target import checks the exact plan fingerprint, rejects existing unknown or changed state and verifies each batch before publishing completion; explicit stopped-writer handoff remains a deployment prerequisite

limitations: Review is scoped to the frozen Rust implementation and these executable boundaries
No production storage, provider call or managed migration is performed by this lane

observations: Read original upstream 4ed0267b5a081ac4884431fd7f5ef41fce20a4d1 Python change and integration assertions. Rust reserve and renewal call LocalControl.update, which delegates to update_locked; progress takes the same per-investigation writer. The three Rust cases exercise reserve, renewal, and settlement under four active independent progress writers and verify persistence, bounded completion, budget/job costs and renewed expiry. This is behavior regression coverage, not literal copying of the PostgreSQL blocking test.

Publication includes writer ownership revision in the same fenced KeeperMap update as Lens data and writer release. Prepared blobs alone do not advance published state. Missing or mismatched published payloads fail closed.

Storage transport forces strict KeeperMap mode, synchronous inserts and query completion; source/hash verification and fresh state tests include stale writer, compaction, atomic multi-record publication, restart and tombstone boundaries.

Progress revalidates job, worker, attempt, running status and live lease after waiting. Eval completion validates matching live scoring token, seals run and clears scoring index with one state commit.

Migration reads eight legacy Lens groups within a REPEATABLE READ READ ONLY PostgreSQL transaction; target rejects unknown published state, requires equal plan report/fingerprint on resume, verifies each chunk and marks completion last.
